key_insight: The paper shows how to trace which instruction words control specific speech characteristics in style-captioned text-to-speech systems. By adapting cross-attention attribution to speech diffusion models, it reveals token-level influence on generated audio and helps explain controllability failures.
problem_solved: Style-captioned TTS can follow natural-language style prompts, but it is unclear how individual words in the instruction affect acoustic properties like speaking style, prosody, or emphasis. This lack of interpretability makes it hard to debug errors and improve controllable speech generation.
method: Adapt DAAM-style cross-attention attribution from vision-language models to speech diffusion models.
Apply the method to CapSpeech-TTS to produce per-token heatmaps over 25 layers of the model.
Analyze token-level attention patterns to understand how style instructions map onto generated speech characteristics.
impact: This gives researchers and practitioners a practical way to inspect and debug style-conditioned TTS models. It can improve transparency, identify failure modes in instruction following, and guide better prompt design for expressive speech synthesis.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing instruction text flowing into a diffusion TTS model with cross-attention attribution overlays.
Token heatmaps highlighting which words influence different speech segments or acoustic features.
A layer-wise visualization summarizing attribution across 25 model layers.
Before/after examples comparing spoken output under different style captions.
paper_title: How Do Instructions Shape Speech? Cross-Attention Attribution for Style-Captioned Text-to-Speech
paper_authors: Nityanand Mathur, Hamees Sayed, Wasim Madha, Apoorv Singh, Sameer Khurana
